findings.reason: §16 supersedes one named §13 rule but its unqualified "every launch" silently supersedes a second one, so a worker implementing it literally makes the in-harness door reserve and lock the run; the section must state that the in-harness door stays exempt and say why.
findings.text: §16's headline rule "Every launch takes one, held until its own launch ends" contradicts §13's constraint at :165 that "In-harness launches take no reservation and respect one", and the landed code still carries `refuse_held_launch` (dispatch_launch.py:2445, whose docstring states an in-harness launch "takes no reservation of its own") precisely because nothing on disk records the end of the session an in-harness launch attaches to — a reservation it took could never be freed, leaving that run unlaunchable for good

findings.reason: §16's own purpose is that a launch which dies mid-composition names the attempt it was making; the plan must add a step rewriting the marker from the reservation and a case asserting the marker's attempt equals the reserved one, or the repair is incomplete on the case it was written for.
findings.text: §16 fixes `launch_reservation_key` to read the attempt marker's own number, but only "with only the marker": once any `attempt-N` receipt exists the key is the newest receipt plus one, which can differ from the attempt the marker was written with, because the marker records the ledger-derived number at dispatch.py:2774 (from `attempt = int(previous_attempt) + 1` at :2755) and the reservation block at :2864 then reassigns `attempt = reservation.attempt` without rewriting `attempt.json` — so in exactly the run shape §13 exists for (an earlier attempt with no ledger row, e.g. nova's run standing at attempt 5 with none) the marker names an attempt the launch never runs and can duplicate an existing `attempt-N` receipt, which defeats the attribution §16 repairs for the solo-shadow case

response_events.note: §16 now exempts the in-harness door: it still takes no reservation and respects one, as §13 states, because nothing on disk records the end of the session it attaches to, so a reservation it took could never be freed. 'Every launch' is narrowed to every launch that spawns a supervisor.

§16 now rewrites the marker with the reserved attempt whenever the reservation block reassigns it, so attempt.json always names the attempt the launch runs and never duplicates an existing attempt-N receipt; a case covers a run with an earlier attempt and no ledger row.
